goal: A gitleaks secret scan of the commit range origin/main..HEAD runs in the lefthook pre-push hook and in the lint CI job, and docs/runbooks/secrets-rotation-api-keys.md records the 2026-09-20 rotations and the decision not to scrub git history.
non_goals: No git history rewrite (no git filter-repo, no force-push). The decision not to scrub is recorded, not executed.
No full-history scan in the gate. The range is origin/main..HEAD only, so commit 24353cf1c needs no allowlist entry.
No key rotation, and no read of any live secret value. The rotation rows are owner-reported.
No test of the exposed old keys against providers.
No use of the gitleaks GitHub Action (it needs a paid license for organization repositories). CI downloads a pinned release binary.
No pre-commit hook. The scan runs pre-push, as the ticket states.
No change to claude.yml or claude-code-review.yml.
user_visible_behavior: Developer: pnpm ci:secret-scan runs gitleaks on the commits in origin/main..HEAD with redaction on, and exits non-zero on a finding.

Developer: git push runs the scan through lefthook. A machine without the gitleaks binary FAILS the hook and prints the install command (brew install gitleaks). git push --no-verify stays the escape (owner decision 2026-09-21: hard-fail).
CI: the lint job installs a pinned gitleaks release, verifies its sha256, then runs pnpm ci:secret-scan. A checksum mismatch fails the job.
A secret that one commit adds and a later commit in the same push removes is still reported, because the scan reads commits, not the file tree.

Operator: the Rotation Log has one row each for OPENAI_API_KEY, SERPAPI key, Supabase anon key, the two Upstash tokens and the Stripe test key: date 2026-09-20, actor, secret name, and the text owner-reported; not independently verified; no fingerprint recorded.

Operator: the runbook has a History scrub decision section (decision: no scrub; reason: every exposed value is rotated and dead, a rewrite plus force-push breaks every clone, worktree and open PR for low value; revisit if any exposed value is found live) and a Secret scan section (install, what to do on a finding, how to add an allowlist entry).
docs/audits/2026-07-06-codebase-audit-findings.md item C1 shows the true status of steps 1, 3 and 4.
invariants: gitleaks always runs with --redact. A finding never prints the secret value into a terminal, a CI log, or a transcript.
A gate that cannot see never passes: an absent binary, an unresolvable origin/main, or a gitleaks error exit are all failures, locally and in CI.
src/__tests__/ci-audit-wiring.test.ts stays green: ci:secret-scan is declared in package.json, runs in the lint job of ci.yml, and is mirrored in lefthook.yml.
The CI binary is pinned to an exact version and verified by sha256 before it runs. The checksum table covers each runner.arch the lint job can land on (X64, ARM64).
Every allowlist entry in the gitleaks config has a reason comment. Prefer a value-pattern entry over a path entry; a path entry is only for a file that exists solely as a fixture.
The runbook records fingerprints, dates and evidence only, never a key value.
edge_cases: origin/main..HEAD is empty (HEAD equals origin/main): the scan exits 0 with zero commits scanned, and prints the count so a vacuous pass is visible.
verify-gate.sh and lefthook enumerate every ci:* script, so after this merges each worktree gate runs the scan. The root session installs gitleaks on this machine before it arms this run.

Existing fixtures that look like secrets (sk_test_ strings, JWT-shaped test tokens) are outside the range until a commit touches them. Run one advisory full-tree gitleaks pass during the build to find those classes, and allowlist by value pattern with a reason. Record the result in the deviations file.
The parked self-hosted runner is a Mac-hosted Linux VM (ARM64). The install step selects the asset by runner.arch.
A docs-only PR still runs the lint job, so the scan still runs.
The Supabase anon key is a JWT. The default gitleaks JWT rule covers it; do not disable that rule.
existing_patterns_to_follow: scripts/ci/merge-ledger-audit.ts + scripts/ci/__tests__ — a tsx audit with an injected exec seam and a loud failure when origin/main is absent.
lefthook.yml — one command per audit: run: pnpm ci:<name>.
.github/workflows/ci.yml lint job — one named step per audit; third-party inputs pinned (SHA for actions; version + sha256 for a downloaded binary).
docs/runbooks/secrets-rotation-api-keys.md — the Rotation Log table and its 2026-09-16 row.
test_seams: runSecretScan({ exec, env, log }) exported from scripts/ci/secret-scan.ts, with exec injected.
tests_to_add: fails with the install command when the gitleaks binary is absent
fails when origin/main cannot be resolved
scans the commit range origin/main..HEAD with redaction on
exits non-zero when gitleaks reports a finding
fails closed when gitleaks exits with an error that is not a finding
reports the scanned commit count when the range is empty
includes the secret scan in package, lint CI and local pre-push
rollback_plan: Revert the single squash commit. The hook, the CI step and the script go away together, so the wiring test stays green. The runbook rows are documentation and are safe to keep or revert.
observability: The lint job shows a named Run secret scan step with a non-trivial duration and the scanned commit count.
A recorded drill in the runbook: a scratch repository with a committed-then-deleted fake key fails the scan, and the output shows REDACTED in place of the value.
